beats.say: Fake news often looks like an official decision and spreads fast in group chats.
No source, no date, it rushes you and asks you to send it to everyone.

body.text: All salary cards change from tomorrow!

beats.say: Before sharing, check the news on the organisation's site and in reliable news outlets.
If it is fake, report it to the platform and post a short correction in the group.

scenes.title: News in your chats
scenes.intro: News arrives in your work and family chats. What do you do with each?

body.text: Forwarded. Urgent! From tomorrow civil servants' salary cards are being replaced. Update your details so the old card is not blocked:

steps.say: A colleague posted it, but no source is given.

actions.label: Open link
actions.feedback: This page harvests card details. Accounting announces salary card changes through official channels.

actions.label: Ask accounting
actions.feedback: Right. Check an internal decision with an internal source, on a number you know.

actions.label: Reply: unverified, do not open the link
actions.feedback: Good, you protected your colleagues. Show the message to security as well.

actions.label: Send to family group
actions.feedback: Spreading unchecked news pulls others into the trap.

steps.label: Official: all utility debts written off, registration ends today
steps.say: It looks like a familiar news site. Check the address.

actions.label: Register
actions.feedback: Gündəm24's address is gundem24.example; this is a clone. The form collects personal data.

actions.label: Share
actions.feedback: You would be spreading a cloned site. Check the address and source before sharing.

actions.label: Check the official site
actions.feedback: Right. A decision like this would be on the organisation's own site.

actions.label: Close tab
actions.feedback: Good. The address was not Gündəm24's real domain.

body.text: Anyone here working in a state office? They say the internet in Baku will be cut for three days from tomorrow. True?

actions.label: Probably true, get ready
actions.feedback: A state employee's word gives news weight. Do not confirm what you do not know.

actions.label: I don't know, I'll check an official source and write back
actions.feedback: Right. An honest "I don't know" stops a false story.

actions.label: Forward to other groups
actions.feedback: You would carry the false story to even more people.

steps.label: Ministry of Social Services: 50 vacancies. Application fee 10 AZN
steps.say: This page was opened in your own ministry's name.

actions.label: Apply
actions.feedback: The ministry charges no application fee. The fake page collects people's money and data.

actions.label: Report to platform
actions.feedback: Right. Tell the press office too so it can publish an official warning.

actions.label: Tell the press office
actions.feedback: Great. Report the page to the platform too so it is removed faster.

actions.label: Skip it, not my job
actions.feedback: The fake page cheats people in your office's name. Reporting takes a minute.

scenes.prompt: Match each doubt with the right check.

pairs.left: The photo looks familiar and old
The site looks like a familiar news site
pairs.right: Compare the address with the real domain

pairs.left: The story scares and rushes you

scenes.explain: A few seconds of checking can stop a false story from reaching thousands.

nodes.text: This morning you posted the "salary cards are changing" story in the family group. At noon you learned it is fake.

choices.label: I delete it and post a correction
choices.feedback: Right. A correction stops those who already saw it.

choices.label: I delete it quietly
choices.feedback: People who saw it may already be passing it on. A short correction breaks the chain.

choices.label: I do nothing, it's too late
choices.feedback: It is not too late: a correction still stops the spread.

nodes.text: I opened that link and typed in my card details. What do I do now?
nodes.speaker: Your relative
nodes.spoken: I opened that link and typed in my card details. <breath> What do I do now?

choices.label: Call the bank on the number on your card now and block the card
choices.feedback: Right. The sooner the card is blocked, the lower the risk of losing money.

choices.label: Don't worry, maybe nothing will happen
choices.feedback: Scammers often use card details right away.

choices.label: Delete what you typed on the site
choices.feedback: The details are already with the scammer. Only the bank can block the card.

question.prompt: A journalist messages you: "Can you comment on your ministry's decision?" What do you do?

options.label: I refer them to the press office
options.feedback: Right. Only the press office speaks for the organisation.

options.label: I say what I know
options.feedback: A half-informed comment can become new false news, and the "journalist" may be fake too.

options.label: I send a photo of the internal document
options.feedback: Internal documents must not be shared, and a photo can spread without context.

scenes.explain: Official comments come from the press office. That protects you and the organisation.

points: Check the source on the organisation's own site before sharing.
Do not confirm news you are unsure of; the press office speaks for the organisation.
Report fake pages and news; if you shared by mistake, post a correction.
